options: It is supported by police records showing that authorities rarely arrested capoeira practitioners.
It correctly explains why the berimbau has only a single string.
It is doubtful, because historical records indicate that authorities understood capoeira to be a form of fighting.
It applies to the nineteenth century but not to the period when capoeira first developed.
explanation: Choice C is the best answer because Okoye-Santos argues that police records showing arrests of practitioners 'specifically as fighters' indicate that authorities 'plainly recognized what they were seeing,' undermining the disguise explanation. Choice A reverses what the records show. Choice B is unrelated to her argument, and Choice D draws a distinction between periods that the text does not make.

Mehra argues that future rovers on Mars should rely on power sources other than solar panels.

Bao argues that wind farms cool the air above them by more than they warm the ground, producing a net cooling effect.

passage: At the royal court of Yogyakarta, on the Indonesian island of Java, the sacred bedhaya dance was for centuries passed on only from teacher to pupil, and when court scribes in the late nineteenth century began recording its choreography in written notation, some observers predicted that the dance would thereby be fixed in a definitive form. Choice A has no basis in the comparison, and Choice D makes a claim about astronauts' arm bones for which the text gives no data.

Because the coins were found near Australia, they must have been carried there by Southeast Asian sailors rather than by Swahili traders.

passage: The compression method that computer scientist Valentina Rossi and her colleagues in Montevideo, Uruguay, first sketched on a whiteboard in 2019, then refined over three years of testing on satellite images of the Río de la Plata estuary, and finally ______ in a 2022 paper reduces file sizes by nearly half without discarding any data.

passage: At the ruins of a caravanserai—a roadside inn for traveling merchants—in the Zeravshan Valley of present-day Uzbekistan, archaeologist Dilnoza Rakhimova uncovered coins from many distant places: bronze coins from China, silver coins from Persia, and gold coins from the Byzantine Empire. question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

produced its own coins in bronze, silver, and gold.
was abandoned soon after it was constructed.

passage: Five handwritten copies survive of a tenth-century table of star positions first compiled by an astronomer in Isfahan, in present-day Iran. question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

were copied directly from the copy made in Cairo.
were made before the oldest copy, which is kept in Isfahan.
contain no other mistakes in their star positions.

passage: The Swedish island of Gotland has no silver deposits of its own, yet hundreds of Viking Age hoards of silver have been discovered there. minted coins that were later copied in Baghdad.
was connected, directly or through intermediaries, to exchange networks reaching far beyond Scandinavia.
was rarely visited by people from mainland Sweden.

passage: In the West African city of Timbuktu, in present-day Mali, many families have preserved handwritten manuscripts for centuries. actively read and studied by many people over a long period.
all written by the same author.
brought to Timbuktu only in recent years.

passage: Iron left in contact with oxygen and water slowly forms rust. Chemistry student Kenji Morimoto placed identical iron nails in three sealed jars. The first jar held only dry air. only when nails are of a certain size.
only when it is not sealed inside a container.
when oxygen and water are both present.

passage: In the rainforests of Borneo, fig trees of different species produce fruit at different times of the year rather than all in one season. grow only in places where hornbills build their nests.
produce fruit that hornbills and gibbons usually avoid.

passage: Many chameleon species in Madagascar can change color. Herpetologist Hery Rakotomalala watched males of one species in the wild. help the chameleon warm itself in the sun.

passage: The old city of Shibam in Yemen is known for its tall houses of mud brick, many five or more stories high. is explained by the fact that it never rains in Shibam.
happened because the towers were eventually rebuilt in stone.

confused reindeer with other kinds of livestock.

is used up as it reacts with hydrogen peroxide.

releases oxygen from its own atoms when placed in solution.

passage: Khipus—bundles of knotted cords used for record keeping in the Inca Empire of South America—were made from different fibers. the frogs fed forest ants to grow larger than those fed fruit flies.

resulted from ichthyosaurs' coughing up fish bones more often than cephalopod hooks.

a workshop where clay cups were made for sale.
home to a wealthy family.

made without any measuring tools.
written only in years of drought.

natural hiding places such as rock crevices are scarce.
coconut trees grow underwater.
octopuses rarely need to hide.

have seen these lakes disappear completely.

are protected from floods by the glaciers above them.

images of an animal the artists had never seen.
at least about 3,000 years old.

lived far from any roads or rivers.

was likely written out by someone other than the monk, such as a student recording his words.
proves that the monk's tremor disappeared in his final years.

uses the antifungal compound mainly as a source of energy.

the region received less rainfall 10,000 years ago than it does today.
stalagmites in the cave grow fastest during dry periods.
the region was considerably wetter between 10,000 and 6,000 years ago than it has been since.

long-established pairs sing duets more often than newly formed pairs do.
gibbons sing duets mainly to attract new mates.
newly formed pairs avoid singing until they can coordinate their phrases.

the mounds' higher nutrient levels, not just their extra moisture, help explain the thicker grass.
termites feed mainly on the grasses that grow on their mounds.

residents no longer value traditional customs of any kind.

fish were shared according to custom long before seals were.

accurately describes the market women whose cases Mensah studied.
was based mainly on the same court records that Mensah examined.

a large city could be supplied with food from land close to it.

one khipu combined totals drawn from the other five.

most of the dust in the ice came from Antarctica itself.
winds were weaker and land surfaces were wetter than during warmer periods.
winds were stronger, land in the dust's source regions was drier, or both.

held fermentation at a standstill until spring, so that the kimchi remained essentially unchanged through the winter.
shielded the kimchi from cold nights and thereby favored the bacteria that acidify cabbage most quickly.

question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

uplift, rather than climate, was most likely the principal driver of the river's incision.
uplift and climatic change contributed roughly equally to the incision, since both were operating during the period.
the adjacent block of crust must have experienced a different climate from that of the river's watershed.

marked the point at which the shelter's occupants stopped using ochre from the nearby deposit.
reflected a preference for the distant pigment rather than a lack of accessible local ochre.
shows that the northern mine was unknown to people in the region before about 5,000 years ago.

question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

because Barents Sea walruses yielded ivory of higher quality than Greenland walruses did.
because overall European demand for walrus ivory collapsed during that century.
less because of falling European demand than because of competition from a source nearer to Europe.

reflects the greater difficulty of opening the fruit found in Forest A.
would disappear if Forest B orangutans were simply housed together at a rehabilitation center.

a rain that prompts germination is often not followed by enough moisture for seedlings to mature.
seeds that germinate after the first rain rarely sprout at all.
seedlings are able to survive prolonged drought after germinating.
